issues.body: When BUCKET is unset, only PRINT_POLICY_ONLY avoids account discovery; ordinary --dry-run executes `aws sts get-caller-identity` before reaching the dry-run command wrapper. This contradicts both the script/README promise that `bootstrap-bench-iam.sh --dry-run` makes no AWS call and the safety purpose of previewing exact commands before using credentials. The test is vacuous for the documented invocation because it always adds `--bucket`, bypassing this branch.
issues.fix_hint: Make ordinary dry-run use a clearly marked placeholder account/bucket (as --print-policy does), or print the STS lookup as a prospective command without executing it. Add a hermetic test invoking --dry-run with no --bucket and assert the AWS stub log remains empty.
issues.title: --dry-run performs an AWS STS call unless --bucket is supplied

issues.body: The script claims the whole bootstrap is idempotent, but `add-role-to-instance-profile` is wrapped only by a generic error-string allowlist. AWS reports an already occupied one-role instance profile as a limit/quota error rather than one of the accepted AlreadyExists strings, so a normal second run can terminate under `set -e`. The hermetic test only checks that the command is printed and does not exercise rerun behavior.
issues.fix_hint: Before attaching, query `get-instance-profile` and skip when ROLE_NAME is already present; fail explicitly if a different role occupies the profile. Add stubbed first-run and rerun cases that verify the same role is a no-op and a conflicting role fails clearly.
issues.title: Re-running bootstrap can fail when the role is already attached

verdict.summary: The durable-egress integration is generally careful, but the bootstrap's advertised no-call dry-run behavior is not true for the documented default invocation. The hermetic test supplies --bucket and therefore misses the real path. The bootstrap also appears not to be idempotent at the role/profile attachment step, contrary to its contract.
